verified: Richard Paisner's shareholder suit challenges the U.S. government's 10% stake in Intel, and Tom's Hardware, citing Wired, reports that unsealed case documents include internal notes of Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro warning that rejecting the offer would have "consequences"; the complaint also alleges a conflict of interest involving Intel adviser Skadden Arps (Bloomberg Law). The 10% government stake itself is confirmed (The Verge).
unconfirmed: That Trump personally directed the pressure, that the stake was an unlawful quid pro quo for the $8.9 billion in CHIPS Act funds, and that Intel's outside counsel provided $100 million in free legal services — these rest on the complaint's allegations and Wired's review, not on a court finding or independent confirmation.

verified: 少数股东 Richard Paisner 已就美国政府取得 Intel 10% 股权一事起诉 Intel（3DNews 援引《金融时报》报道，LegalClarity 汇总的 Bloomberg Law 报道亦确认该诉讼）；诉状指控公司 CEO 与董事会在交易前受到美国政府施压，并指出为 Intel 提供交易咨询的世达律师事务所（Skadden, Arps）存在利益冲突；The Verge 报道确认联邦政府确实持有了 Intel 10% 股份。
unconfirmed: Tom's Hardware 援引《连线》（Wired）查阅的已解封文件称，商务部律师 David Shapiro 曾对 Intel 首席财务官表示“不要以为这是一场谈判”，并称拒绝“后果无法预料”——这些引述仅来自单家媒体的文件解读，法庭尚未认定；白宫以解冻 89 亿美元 CHIPS 法案资金作为交换条件、Intel 外部律师提供高达 1 亿美元免费法律服务以换取免于行政令，均属诉状与匿名消息源的说法，未经独立证实；法院亦未就 10% 股权是否违法作出任何裁决。

titles.en: Intel shareholder lawsuit alleges Trump pressured board into 10% stake
titles.zh: Intel 股东诉讼指控白宫施压换取 10% 股权
